R101.note: Uses the correct AuthorizeAsync pattern but authorizes against a named policy "AdminOnly" that is not shown as registered anywhere (root Roles="Admin" is used elsewhere); write-up discloses this dependency, but if unregistered AuthorizeAsync throws and blocks even legitimate admins, not just attackers.

R102.note: path.basename() does not fully close traversal: verified path.basename('..') returns '..', so name=='..' still yields require('./plugins/..'), escaping the intended directory by one level; no harm to legitimate names otherwise.

R103.note: Switching GET to POST is directionally right but the write-up's stated reason is wrong for this controller (no [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]/antiforgery filter is added or shown configured; ASP.NET Core does not implicitly validate antiforgery tokens on plain API-style POST actions), so real CSRF protection is not actually implemented, only an incidental SameSite-cookie mitigation; verb change itself is the required fix and doesn't restrict legitimate use.

R104.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the identical pattern used by every sibling admin route; no other behavior change.

R105.note: Loads the message and checks AuthorUserId ownership before delete, failing via HubException; matches existing SendMessage identity pattern, no side effects.

R106.note: Shell invocation fully eliminated via archive/tar, closing CWE-78 well, but the stated contract requires continuing to use the request context for cancellation and the rewritten ListArchive silently never checks ctx (parameter is now unused), a behavior change not mentioned in the write-up.

R107.note: Extension now derived from file-type's detected.ext instead of client-supplied originalname, matching the already-validated MIME allowlist; no new restriction beyond the fix itself.

R108.note: Replaces PowerShell process spawn entirely with native Ping class, eliminating the injection surface; output format is an approximation of Test-Connection text, openly stated in the write-up, not a functional restriction.

R109.note: ECB replaced with AESGCM (authenticated, nonce-based); ciphertext format change (nonce prefix) is disclosed and necessary for the fix, no other consumer shown in scope.

R110.note: Standard @Lazy self-injection pattern routes the call through the AOP proxy so @PreAuthorize is actually evaluated; restores originally-intended ADMIN-only enforcement, no unrelated behavior change.

R111.note: Replaces the eval'd string with a closure capturing the same arguments; same recordReminder call semantics, and incidentally fixes a latent quoting bug in the original string-building for messages containing quotes.

R112.note: Uses Express's documented root option on sendFile, the canonical fix for this exact sink; behavior for legitimate filenames is unchanged.

R113.note: execFile with an argument array closes the reported shell metacharacter injection cleanly; residual argument/flag-injection risk (a domain value starting with '-') is not addressed but is a distinct, lesser weakness than the reported CWE-78 vector, which is fully closed.

R114.note: Adds an ownership comparison against the server-loaded invoice's AccountId and returns NotFound for both missing and unauthorized cases exactly per the stated contract; no other change.

R115.note: Enabling @EnableMethodSecurity is the correct root fix restoring @PreAuthorize enforcement; the added canManageUser check is only an existence check mislabeled as resource-level authorization in the explanation, but it doesn't reject any legitimate account or add real restriction, so it's harmless.
